analytical_question: As of October 13, 2026, what is the conditional creative-destruction exposure of a hypothetical fieldwork-led consulting firm applying human-reviewed LLM market research to Chinese home/lifestyle brands entering the US, and what should management do in its next 12 months?
general_et_finding: As of October 13, 2026, human-directed LLM generation can plausibly assist bilingual public-source synthesis and drafting, subject to grounding, privacy and review risks [S1,S4]. The NBER November 2023 finding is from customer support, not consultancy economics. Schumpeter-style value creation and possible displacement are credible mechanisms; Christensen-style disruption is conditional upon an actual new-market/low-end foothold and movement into incumbent customers, NOT proven here [C1]. It may be sustaining when integrated into incumbent work, disruptive if it enables acceptable self-service alternatives. Neither adoption timing nor substitution can be inferred from model capability alone.
application_finding: At the application level, LLM-generated public-source market mapping can lower some research preparation effort, but cannot establish firsthand US customer needs or true channel suitability; market advice remains contingent on human verification [S3,S4]. Creative-destruction ledger (hypothetical scenario, not observations). 1. Element: bilingual public-source desk research; creation/enabling: Create: quicker desk preparation, interview-guide drafts, source-linked market hypothesis lists [S1 inference, A1 assumption]; displacement/reduction: Displace: lower-value desk-research hours and standalone briefing line items; possible price pressure on supporting deliverables [A1 scenario only]; affected stakeholders: research participants, fieldwork staff, customers, local partners and principals; mechanism: rapid draft/synthesis lowers possible production effort but introduces source-review/rework; timing: possible during 2026–27 pilot, observed impact date unknown; uncertainty: no measured cost, quality or substitution. 2. Element: authentic US consumer and channel validation; creation: AI can draft hypotheses and prompts for humans [S3]; displacement: it does NOT replace witnessed interviews, consent, partner diligence or sales-channel execution by the bounded technology; affected stakeholders: clients, participants and field partners; timing: ongoing pilot and future unknown; uncertainty: whether buyers pay for verification is unmeasured. 3. Element: information integrity and governance; creation: traceable evidence workflow; displacement/cannibalization: review time may offset draft-time savings [S4]; stakeholders: clients, research subjects, reviewers; time: immediate use; uncertainty: error and rework rates not measured. No net-benefit conclusion follows.
organization_specific_finding: Business-model baseline: Scenario baseline (October 13, 2026): hypothetical small bilingual consultancy selling supervised US customer interviews, field validation, partner diligence and channel-entry execution. Paid projects and execution retainers depend mainly on authentic field access, recruitment, consent and follow-through; desk research supports the service but is not its core sold deliverable. Business-Model Disruption Potency: Moderate conditional task/service exposure: AI may commoditize the supporting research portion, but cannot itself conduct authentic interviews or secure channel execution under this defined capability. Actual organization-wide disruption potency remains Undetermined pending fee mix, channel trust, client switching and competitor data; Moderate is a reasoned scenario, not an observed loss. Severity/time placement: Moderate scenario severity for supporting reports; actual business-model severity and timing undetermined. The 2026–27/2027–29/later buckets are planning conventions only. An illustrative Moderate/near cell would call for pilot or partner, but is NOT an evidence-backed impact forecast.

evidence.claim: A reported productivity gain for AI-assisted customer support, not an estimated consulting gain
evidence.source_or_reference: S1: Brynjolfsson, Li & Raymond, Generative AI at Work, NBER WP 31161, revised November 2023, https://www.nber.org/papers/w31161
evidence.date_or_recency: November 2023 revision; reviewed evidence snapshot October 13, 2026
evidence.notes: 5,179 support agents; reported mean 14% higher issues resolved/hour, 34% for novices; no transfer of those percentages to consulting, margins, employment or substitution.

evidence.claim: Existing-source research and direct consumer research serve distinct information needs
evidence.source_or_reference: S3: US Small Business Administration, Market Research and Competitive Analysis, https://www.sba.gov/counseling/plan-your-business/#market-research
evidence.notes: Desk sources may lack audience specificity; interviews and focus groups offer direct but costly evidence; this does not prove willingness to pay for local services.

evidence.claim: Generative AI can produce misleading assertions and poses privacy and overreliance risks
evidence.source_or_reference: S4: NIST AI 600-1, Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile, July 2024, https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/ai/NIST.AI.600-1.pdf
evidence.notes: Sections 2.2, 2.4 and 2.7; proposed human review is a control, not proof that errors vanish.

evidence.claim: Creative destruction, sustaining/disruptive mechanisms, incumbent dilemma and threat matrix
evidence.source_or_reference: C1: Fortino, Mastering the Craft of Emerging Technology Adoption, Chapter 1, sections 1.2–1.7, Figure 1.8 (course reading)
evidence.notes: Used for analytical categories and matrix actions; does not establish case-specific forecast.

evidence.claim: The organizations and their revenue/capability assumptions are hypothetical inputs
evidence.source_or_reference: A1: student-selected case context supplied in all three run packets
evidence.notes: No observed client willingness to pay, market substitution, margins, consumer interviews or verified field-network advantage. HBS 403 excluded.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: Sustaining/complementary alternative: firms may use AI to strengthen professionally verified deliverables without changing what clients purchase; AI-produced drafts may increase verification costs.
The NBER customer-support productivity study is not direct evidence of consultancy savings or client switching; HBS study was unavailable (403) and is not cited as evidence.
Hypothetical organizations have no observed revenues, profit margins, buyers, price elasticity or validated competitive pressure. Course historical examples guide method, not forecast.
confidence_and_uncertainty: General task-assistance/risk mechanism: moderate confidence in plausible assistance and documented model risks, low confidence in transfer size. Firm baseline: explicit hypothetical assumptions, not empirically verified. Potency: Moderate conditional task/service exposure: AI may commoditize the supporting research portion, but cannot itself conduct authentic interviews or secure channel execution under this defined capability. Actual organization-wide disruption potency remains Undetermined pending fee mix, channel trust, client switching and competitor data; Moderate is a reasoned scenario, not an observed loss. Severity: scenario-dependent. Timing: undetermined; near/mid/far date bins are conventions only, and neither a 2027–2029 impact claim nor a probability is substantiated. Do not equate unknown with Low.
value_opportunity_implication: Create: quicker desk preparation, interview-guide drafts, source-linked market hypothesis lists; realization requires accurate source tracing, acceptable review cost and measured user/client value. New underserved clientele and revenue are hypotheses, not established effects.
risk_governance_implication: Incumbent dilemma: Management could cannibalize supporting report charges while defending consentful field recruitment and partner follow-through. Moving early can degrade trust, invite privacy exposure or create uncompensated checking; moving late can make ancillary briefings uncompetitive. Field advantage is a hypothesis, not a proven moat. NIST [S4] identifies confabulation, privacy and overreliance risks; use human accountability, source checks and approved public data, not synthetic consumer interviews. These controls require testing, not presumed effectiveness. No legal, tax, customs or product-compliance decisions within scope.
recommendation_management_implication: Matrix action: Moderate scenario severity for supporting reports; actual business-model severity and timing undetermined. The 2026–27/2027–29/later buckets are planning conventions only. An illustrative Moderate/near cell would call for pilot or partner, but is NOT an evidence-backed impact forecast. Bounded response: Pilot/partner narrowly as a process-control experiment, not a claim of urgent core-model rescue: operations lead tests public-data research prep against prior process; require documented consent for any field interviews, human review, no client-sensitive material in unapproved tools; measure all-in hours, accuracy and field execution quality before changing fees. Pilot acceptance/stop thresholds must be agreed by owner before kickoff based on baseline measurement, including denominator, audit sample and review date; no fabricated percentages or predeclared success.
change_monitoring_triggers: Operations lead reviews quarterly: monitor separately (a) share of invoice value for desk-only research and (b) percentage of clients requesting self-service AI briefs; calibrate thresholds on observed baseline, and reconsider potency if core fieldwork retainers are lost to AI-enabled alternatives.

Review source freshness, material AI error/rework and client data incidents at each pilot checkpoint; any material confidentiality breach pauses use pending human review. Proposed monitoring rules are managerial controls, not verified market thresholds.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Breakdown of paid report work versus field execution and retention
